policy_name: SAP AI Ethics Handbook (Development Chapter): Handbook for applying SAP's Global AI Ethics Policy across the AI Factory Process
issuing_authority: SAP SE (Global Head of Artificial Intelligence / AI Ethics Office)
geo_constraints: SAP and all its employees worldwide; applies to SAP software solutions including embedded third-party AI systems

locale_context.regulation: Self-regulation · internal AI ethics policy applied through a development-process handbook
locale_context.culture: European enterprise-software self-governance anchored in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and data-protection practice: red lines, risk classification and an AI Ethics Steering Committee embedded in a staged product-development process.

key_dates.event: Updated version of the handbook (cover: 'Updated version: August 2023')

versions.title: Updated version: August 2023
versions.summary: Only one version recorded for this policy.
versions.note: The cover calls this an 'Updated version', so an earlier edition exists, but its date is not stated in the document.

covered_entities: SAP employees involved in development, deployment and sale of AI systems
covered_systems: rule-based and learning-based AI systems in SAP products
third-party AI systems embedded in SAP solutions
covered_activities: AI use-case ideation, validation, realization, productization and operations (AI Factory Process)
risk classification of AI use cases
conditions: Red-line use cases must be stopped immediately

High-risk use cases (personal/sensitive data, automated decision-making, negative effects on individuals, high-risk sectors) require AI Ethics Steering Committee assessment before further development, deployment or sale
objective: Guide SAP employees in applying SAP's Global AI Ethics Policy at every stage of the AI development lifecycle, so that AI systems are developed, deployed and sold in line with SAP's ethical guiding principles.

related_policies.policy: SAP Data Protection and Privacy (DPP) policy and product standards DPP-350 / DPP-361

conflict_rule: Disclaimer: the handbook is a general guide and does not replace existing or new processes, policies or procedures; employees must also adhere to other policies such as the DPP policy and product development standards.

record_provenance.notes: Text taken from the copy in asago-ai/asago-policy-mapper (policy_examples/sap.pdf). The document is the 'Development Chapter' of the SAP AI Ethics Handbook (marked 'External'), dated 'Updated version: August 2023'; it applies, rather than reproduces in full, the SAP Global AI Ethics Policy, whose own text and date were not consulted. Classified internal_policy/enforceable because it sets out the policy's mandatory requirements (red lines, high-risk assessment, 'shall' duties) for all SAP employees, although its disclaimer calls it a general guide that does not replace policies; binding=false (corporate policy, not law). Whether a newer edition exists is unknown. The PDF uses a two-column layout; the -layout extraction interleaves columns, so clause text was checked against a plain pdftotext extraction. Requirements repeat across the five AI Factory stages; section references give the first stage where each appears.

clauses.section: Red Lines – SAP Red Line Cases
clauses.original_text: No SAP AI use cases should fall under the so-called Red Lines defined in the SAP AI Ethics Policy. These are defined as highly unethical under the purposes for AI. If your use case is built for these purposes, you are required to immediately stop developing, deploying, and selling that use case.
clauses.object: AI use cases falling under SAP Red Lines (human surveillance, discrimination, deanonymization, manipulation, undermining debate, environmental harm)
clauses.requirement: no SAP AI use case may fall under a red line; such use cases must be stopped immediately
clauses.condition: if the use case is built for a red-line purpose
clauses.purpose: prevent highly unethical uses of AI
clauses.interpretation_notes: Wording taken from the asago copy (sap.pdf), re-extracted without -layout because the two-column layout interleaves text; line-break hyphenation repaired. Red lines listed alongside: human surveillance targeting individuals or groups (biometrics, facial recognition) to disregard or abuse their rights; discriminatory purposes; deanonymization of anonymized data; manipulation for deception; systems undermining human debate or democratic electoral systems; environmental harm; intentionally harmful impacts.

clauses.section: High Risk – SAP High Risk Cases
clauses.original_text: High-risk use cases are not prohibited within SAP; however, they must first go through an assessment process of the AI Ethics Steering Committee before they can be further developed, deployed, and sold.
clauses.requirement: Steering Committee assessment before further development, deployment or sale of high-risk use cases
clauses.condition: use case classified high-risk (personal or sensitive personal data, automated decision-making, negative effects on individuals, high-risk domain)
clauses.affected_asset: individuals affected by AI use cases
clauses.interpretation_notes: Wording taken from the asago copy (sap.pdf), re-extracted without -layout because the two-column layout interleaves text; line-break hyphenation repaired. High-risk domains named include categorisation of natural persons, critical infrastructure, employment/HR, healthcare, private and public services, law enforcement, migration and democratic processes. Use cases with anonymized data sets are not high-risk.

clauses.original_text: AI systems shall be subject to appropriate human oversight, and the rights and freedoms of a human shall exceed that of AI systems. In situations where humans may be directly impacted by a decision made by SAP’s AI system, human oversight shall be introduced to safeguard that AI system does not undermine human autonomy or introduce unintended consequences.
clauses.object: AI systems making decisions that directly impact humans
clauses.requirement: appropriate human oversight; humans can overrule AI decisions
clauses.condition: where humans may be directly impacted by an AI decision
clauses.purpose: protect human autonomy and avoid unintended consequences
clauses.affected_asset: human autonomy; rights and freedoms of affected persons
clauses.interpretation_notes: Wording taken from the asago copy (sap.pdf), re-extracted without -layout because the two-column layout interleaves text; line-break hyphenation repaired. Repeated (in the reverse order) in the Validation stage. Governance mechanism (human-in-the-loop, on-the-loop, in-command) chosen case by case; summary bullet: 'Decisions by an AI system may always be overruled by a human.'

clauses.original_text: Where applicable, when interacting directly with humans (including via Conversational AI or ‘Chatbots’): AI systems shall be made identifiable as such to appropriate end users. AI systems shall be developed such that it does not encourage humans to develop attachment and/or empathy of users towards the AI system. AI systems shall clearly signal to end users that its social interaction is simulated.
clauses.object: AI systems interacting directly with humans, including chatbots
clauses.requirement: disclose AI identity and avoid fostering attachment or empathy towards the AI system
clauses.condition: where applicable, when AI interacts directly with humans
clauses.purpose: transparency and protection against misleading social interaction
clauses.affected_asset: end users' autonomy and informed interaction
clauses.interpretation_notes: Wording taken from the asago copy (sap.pdf), re-extracted without -layout because the two-column layout interleaves text; line-break hyphenation repaired. Repeated in the Validation stage.

clauses.original_text: SAP shall endeavour to detect unfairly biased outputs and shall implement technical and/or organizational measures to prevent direct or indirect prejudice, discrimination, or marginalization of groups or individuals, e.g. by reducing bias in training data.
clauses.requirement: bias detection and technical/organisational anti-discrimination measures
clauses.affected_asset: groups and individuals affected by AI outputs
clauses.interpretation_notes: Wording taken from the asago copy (sap.pdf), re-extracted without -layout because the two-column layout interleaves text; line-break hyphenation repaired. Repeated in Realization, Productization and Operations; related duties: inclusive and representative training data and, where feasible, a fairness function to test for unbiased output. 'Endeavour to detect' is softer than the duty to implement measures.

clauses.original_text: In alignment and compliance with applicable data protection and privacy law, AI systems that engage in profiling or automated decision-making must be able to provide explanations to the extent possible to data subjects upon request, describing the data segment the subject was placed into and the reasons they were placed there. In addition, the reasons as to why the decision was made shall be provided if requested by the data subject. The explanation must be such as to provide the data subject grounds to challenge the decision.
clauses.actor: SAP (AI systems engaging in profiling or automated decision-making)
clauses.requirement: explain segment placement and decision reasons so the data subject can challenge the decision
clauses.condition: upon request of the data subject
clauses.purpose: contestability and transparency of automated decisions
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems performing profiling or automated decision-making
clauses.interpretation_notes: Wording taken from the asago copy (sap.pdf), re-extracted without -layout because the two-column layout interleaves text; line-break hyphenation repaired. Repeated in Productization and Operations.
